headline: All majors below the 200-day line; funding turns negative across the big four while whales withdraw Bitcoin to cold storage.
paragraphs: The regime is bear-favoring and uniform. Bitcoin trades at 64,272, down 48.5% from its 12-month high of 124,740 and sitting below the 200-day simple moving average with no golden cross in sight. Ethereum sits at 1,904, off 60.5% from 4,818. Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano all trade below their 200-day lines as well. There is no asset among the majors that has reclaimed the intermediate trend. The one-week price action on Bitcoin and Ethereum is near flat to slightly negative (Bitcoin down 0.93% over seven days, Ethereum down 0.38%), which means the two largest cryptocurrencies are treading water inside a depressed regime rather than accelerating lower. That matters: it suggests the selling pressure has paused, not reversed.

Momentum and trend are diverging in small but specific ways. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 53.1 and MACD sits below signal, painting a neutral-to-tired picture on the largest asset. Ethereum's RSI is 55.5 with MACD below signal as well. However, Solana, BNB, and Doge all show MACD above signal despite prices still below the 200-day, which is a hidden-strength signal: the immediate oscillator is turning while the larger trend has not yet confirmed. XRP and ADA show weakness across both measures, with RSI at 36.8 and 42.8 respectively and MACD below signal, cementing their role as the weakest of the cohort. A reader should note that Cardano has fallen 13.6% over the past seven days and is off 82% from its 12-month high, which distinguishes it sharply from the broad-based wobble elsewhere.

Derivatives positioning shows funding shifting into negative territory, the first structural sign of capitulation in leverage. Bitcoin funding stands at minus 0.7% annualized (minus 0.0007% per 8-hour), Ethereum at minus 1.6% (minus 0.0015% per 8-hour), and Solana at minus 5.6% (minus 0.0052% per 8-hour). When funding turns negative, longs are paying to hold, which happens when shorts are crowded and the curve inverts. That inversion is now live on four of the five tracked assets. Solana is extreme: its funding is the deepest and its long-to-short ratio sits at 2.33, meaning roughly 2.3 longs for every short. By contrast, XRP and Doge show positive funding (9% and 11% annualized, respectively), signaling shorts are still paying, but their long-to-short ratios are even more stretched at 3.66 and 5.2. These are crowded bets, and in a bear regime they are fragile. Open interest remains substantial across the board (BTC 2.09 billion, ETH 1.34 billion, SOL 220 million), meaning plenty of leverage is still in the water.

Whale flows reveal a split between accumulation and distribution. Over the past 24 hours, Bitcoin net moved off exchanges to the tune of 29 million dollars, with the largest single outflow of 176.9 million from Bitstamp. That outflow to cold storage is a hallmark of long-term holders stepping away from the margin or exchange trading population. Simultaneously, the biggest_onto_exchanges data shows 129.9 million in USDT moving to Bitfinex and 94.4 million plus 53.6 million in BTC moving to OKEx, which suggests one cohort of whales is stocking dry powder while another is rotating Bitcoin into derivatives venues. Stablecoin float stands at 306.4 billion, down only 0.59% over 30 days, which is a flat picture: no mass destabilization, no panic liquidation of stables, and no signal of imminent panic-buying. The weekly net flow for Bitcoin shows a four-week sequence of +701 million, +1.07 billion, minus 564 million, and plus 1.71 million, which is erratic but not trending. The past two weeks have moved off exchanges again, suggesting institutional or large holders are taking coins off the trading grid.

The Fear and Greed Index sits at 31 (Fear) with a 30-day range of 25 to 34, which means the crowd is in the fearful band but not at the extreme panic lows seen earlier in the month. The tape does not confirm that fear: major assets are up 1.3 to 2.3% in 24-hour terms, the market cap rose 1.35%, and the divergence between negative funding (a sign that leverage is unwinding) and flat-to-positive micro-moves suggests that fear-driven selling has plateaued and survivors are consolidating. Bitcoin dominance sits at 56.5%, indicating Bitcoin has held its share of total market cap even as alts have corrected harder. Network difficulty rose 0.8% with 705 blocks to retarget, a modest tick up that signals hashpower remains steady despite price weakness.

Watch for a reclaim of the 200-day moving average on Bitcoin and Ethereum as the condition that would signal a regime shift out of bear-favoring territory. Watch Solana's funding: at minus 5.6%, it is the deepest inversion and could snap back sharply if longs capitulate or price stabilizes. Watch the weekly whale flow: if the next two weeks show continued net outflow to cold storage alongside no inflow to exchanges, it would suggest sustained accumulation by large holders despite the bear regime. Watch the ETF flows: Bitcoin has seen 385 million net outflow over the past five sessions with same-direction days at 3, and if that persists, traditional-finance bid is wavering. Ethereum's ETF flows are positive (46.6 million over five sessions), so the divide between the two flagship assets is a tension to monitor.
